original_question: What is the largest constant C such that, for every sufficiently large graph G of order n with lambda(G) > sqrt(floor(n^2/4)), G contains a cycle of every length ell <= (C - epsilon)n for all positive epsilon < C?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 3 (Nikiforov's problem on consecutive cycles).
correct_elements: Your draft is clearly aiming at the right open problem: the asymptotic extremal constant for forcing consecutive cycle lengths in an n-vertex graph above the spectral Mantel threshold sqrt(floor(n^2/4)). It correctly captures the main form of the question: determine the largest constant C for which every sufficiently large graph satisfying the spectral condition contains cycles of all lengths up to about (C-epsilon)n.
missing_details: In the paper's notation, the relevant spectral parameter is the adjacency spectral radius rho(G)=mu(G), not lambda(G); lambda is reserved for Laplacian eigenvalues in the preliminaries.
The ambient class of graphs should be made explicit: finite simple, undirected, unweighted graphs.
The phrase 'graph of order n' should be spelled out as |V(G)|=n.
The quantifiers should be unpacked: one asks for the maximum real constant C such that for every epsilon with 0<epsilon<C, there exists n0=n0(epsilon) so that the conclusion holds for all n>=n0.
The cycle lengths should be stated as integers, explicitly 3<=ell<=floor((C-epsilon)n) or equivalently 3<=ell<=(C-epsilon)n with ell integral.

To make the question stand alone and avoid confusion with nearby problems in the paper, it should be explicit that there are no additional assumptions such as minimum degree, Hamiltonicity, or absence of isolated vertices.
refined_question: What is the maximum real constant C such that, for every epsilon with 0<epsilon<C, there exists n0=n0(epsilon) for which the following holds: whenever G is a finite simple undirected unweighted graph with |V(G)|=n>=n0 and adjacency spectral radius rho(G)>sqrt(floor(n^2/4)), the graph G contains a cycle C_ell for every integer ell satisfying 3<=ell<=(C-epsilon)n?
justification: The draft matches Section 6, Problem 3, rather than the neighboring fixed-length cycle problems in Section 5. The main paper-faithful correction is the operator: the preliminaries distinguish the adjacency spectral radius rho(G)=mu(G) from Laplacian eigenvalues lambda_i(G), so writing lambda(G) is not faithful to the paper's notation. I also made explicit the global graph conventions from the preliminaries and unpacked the asymptotic quantifiers and the integrality/lower bound on cycle lengths. I did not add any extra structural hypothesis, because Problem 3 imposes none. The paragraph immediately after Problem 3 records the current bounds 1/4<=C<=1/2, confirming that the intended target is exactly the best such constant.
